subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Scripted JSONL provider streams plus scripted per-tool-use approval decisions drive end-to-end session tests in both stacks
one_why: Nuance vs pi-8/codex-5: the harness scripts approvals as first-class inputs (SendApprovalResultArgs lists), so approval-gated tool pipelines are testable without a human or model - the approval-script channel is the portable part; chat-cli variant mocks at the client-API layer and asserts hook stdout files.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: New agent framework returns unconditional Allow for ExecuteCmd/SpawnSubagent/Grep/Mkdir - no per-call approval path exists
evidence: crates/agent/src/agent/permissions.rs:62-69; allowed_tools only gates tool exposure at crates/agent/src/agent/mod.rs:1498; no requires_acceptance in crates/agent/src/agent/tools/execute_cmd.rs
one_why: The framework has a full approval protocol (AgentRequest::SendApprovalResult, mod.rs:598-723) but shell execution never enters it; a host embedding this crate gets silent shell by default - exposure-gating is not execution-gating.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Read tools (ls, image_read) are permission-checked against fs_write allowed/denied path lists while the code comment claims fs_read reuse
evidence: crates/agent/src/agent/permissions.rs:47-61 (comment 'Reuse the same settings for fs read' above settings.fs_write.allowed_paths)
one_why: Config that reads one way and binds another: tightening fs_read protects nothing for ls/image_read, tightening fs_write silently blocks reads; exactly the class of bug permission systems get when policy axes are duplicated per tool.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Token-level bash auto-approval: shlex split, dangerous-token scan, per-pipe-segment readonly allowlist, find -exec and grep -P special cases, anchored-regex user allowlist
one_why: Deny-by-default with conservative escalation (multiline, unl-spaced pipes, subshell tokens always ask) and the two nasty cases other subjects miss (find -exec/-delete, grep -P RCE) handled explicitly and tested - the special-case catalogue is the portable artifact, not the readonly list itself.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Char-based degradation: 600K-char warning nags /compact, auto-compaction fires only reactively on ContextWindowOverflow, hard-fail menu as last rung, all disable-able
one_why: Rung-for-rung recovery UX is genuinely good (warning names /compact, /usage, /clear; user can opt out of automation), but counting chars instead of tokens and triggering compaction on provider error rather than projection means the ladder starts climbing one request too late.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Shadow bare-git checkpoint manager: per-turn tagged commits against the work tree with restore/diff/stats and cleanup, no user repo pollution
one_why: Same design family as cline's stash checkpoints but tagged-commit-per-turn gives diff/stats-between-checkpoints for free (compute_stats_between :269, diff :289); the is_git_installed guard plus manual/auto init split (:86-103) is the honest-degradation pattern.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Claude-style blocking hooks (exit 2 returns STDERR to model) with glob matchers incl. @mcp/tool forms, output caps, and an opt-in output cache; zero trust-scoping of hook origin
one_why: Matcher grammar (@git/status, @builtin, *) and timeout/10KB-cap/cache-TTL fields are a tidy hook contract; but hooks are arbitrary commands defined in agent config with no provenance distinction between user and project files, and cached hook output (cache_ttl_seconds) can serve stale pre-approval context.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Delegate tool spawns detached background q-chat processes, one task per agent, JSON state files under workspace subagents dir, coroutine-monitored
one_why: Crash-survivable status via on-disk JSON state beats in-memory subagent registries, and process isolation is real; but no budgets, no resume of the child's conversation after crash, and one-task-per-agent serializes throughput - shape worth copying, lifecycle not finished.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Shipped chat loop, rendering, compaction driver, error UX and test module fused in one 4,699-LOC file
evidence: crates/chat-cli/src/cli/chat/mod.rs total 4699 LOC; state machine error handling :560-1010; mock-driven tests embedded :4032-4600
one_why: The new agent crate shows the team already knows the fix (732-LOC separated loop with protocol channels); meanwhile the shipped loop can only be changed through a file bigger than two anchors' god files combined.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Two complete agent implementations ship side-by-side: 53k-LOC legacy chat loop and a 13k-LOC clean agent-framework crate, each with its own tools, hooks, and MCP code
evidence: Cargo.toml:8-9 members; crates/agent/src/agent/{agent_loop,task_executor,permissions}.rs vs crates/chat-cli/src/cli/chat/{mod.rs,tools/,agent/legacy/}; standalone runner crates/agent/src/cli/run.rs
one_why: Better-documented and better-factored than the cline dual-tree (new stack has its own integration harness), but permission bugs like findings 2-3 live precisely in the seam where the new stack's policy isn't yet wired to anything users run; synthesis should treat framework-crate scores and shipped-product scores as one product.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Full OAuth dance implemented client-side for MCP servers (740 LOC) on top of rmcp with child-process/SSE/streamable-http transports
evidence: crates/chat-cli/src/mcp_client/oauth_util.rs (740 LOC), crates/chat-cli/src/mcp_client/client.rs:1-709; rmcp 0.8 with auth feature at Cargo.toml:137
one_why: Most subjects treat MCP servers as local stdio only; first-class remote-MCP auth is the difference between an MCP checkbox and usable enterprise interop.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: CI test command excludes a crate that does not exist in workspace members, so the primary cargo-test gate may fail as written
evidence: .github/workflows/rust.yml:77 ('--exclude fig_desktop-fuzz') vs Cargo.toml:8-9 (no fig crates in members)
one_why: Migration leftover from the removed desktop stack; static review can't confirm CI status, hence med confidence - but a gate that references a deleted workspace member is the exact drift evals-in-ci discipline is meant to catch.
